previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted with hypotension, lightheadedness, and new hypoxemia. He has a complex history including HCV cirrhosis, portopulmonary hypertension on treprostinil, and awaiting liver transplant. Workup revealed Enterobacter bacteremia from an unclear source, likely contributing to sepsis and hypotension. He also had significant volume overload, evidenced by bilateral leg edema, bibasilar crackles, and elevated BNP, which improved with aggressive diuresis. A right heart catheterization showed mildly elevated pulmonary pressures at 25 mmHg. He responded well to IV cefepime, later transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin, and was weaned off oxygen. His condition stabilized, and he was discharged home with instructions to complete antibiotics, monitor weight, and follow up with pulmonology and primary care.

___ Transthoracic Echocardiogram: 
The left atrium is mildly dilated. The estimated right atrial 
pressure is at least 15 mmHg. Left ventricular wall thickness,

abnormal systolic septal motion/position consistent with right 
ventricular pressure overload. The aortic valve leaflets (3) 
appear structurally normal with good leaflet excursion. There is 
no valvular aortic stenosis. The increased transaortic velocity 
is likely related to high cardiac output. No aortic 
regurgitation is seen. The mitral valve leaflets are 
structurally normal. Mild (1+) mitral regurgitation is seen. 
Moderate [2+] tricuspid regurgitation is seen. There is severe 
pulmonary artery systolic hypertension. There is a minimally 
increased gradient consistent with trivial pulmonic valve 
stenosis. There is a very small pericardial effusion. 
IMPRESSION: Biatrial enlargment. Preserved global and regional 
left ventricular systolic function. Mild resting LVOT 
obstruction. Mildly dilated right ventricle with borderline 
normal global systolic function. Mild mitral regurgitation. 
Moderate tricuspid regurgitation. Severe pulmonary artery 
systolic hypertension.
Compared with the prior study (images reviewed) of ___, 
the severity of pulmonary artery systolic hypertension has 
increased (previously 46 mmHg, now at least 66 mmHg given 
estimated right atrial pressure. Moderate tricuspid

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ year-old gentleman, with HCV cirrhosis 
(complicated by hepatic encephalopathy, varices and ascites) on 
the liver transplant list, portopulmonary hypertension on 
Remodulin infusion pump, admitted with Enterobacter sepsis, with 
hospital course complicated by multifocal pneumonia, ___, and 
recurrent ascites.

ACTIVE ISSUES:
# Enterobacter sepsis: Outpatient blood cultures from ___ and 
___ were positive for pansensitive enterobacter in 4 out of 4 
bottles. Due to septic shock, patient was admitted to the ICU 
and initially started on IV cefepime. On admission systolic 
blood pressures were in the ___ (from baseline in 100s) and 
trended down to ___, requiring initaition of vasopressin and 
levophed. He was also transfused two units PRBCS on ___.  His 
tunneled line was removed, with tip culture positive for 
Enterobacter as well, indicating that this was the likely source 
of his bacteremia.  On admission, diagnostic paracentesis did 
not show clear evidence of SBP; however, it was performed in the 
setting of previous anti-biotic administration. As discussed 
below, CT torso showed evidence of multifocal pneumonia as well. 
After ___, no other blood cultures from this admission 
returned positive.  On ___, a left IJ tunneled line was 
placed for Remodulin infusion.  He was transferred to the 
Transplant Surgery team on ___. Blood pressures improved and 
he was weaned off pressors on ___.  He subsequently remained 
hemodynamically stable.  Right PICC line was placed and left IJ 
was removed on ___ for continued Remodulin treatment.  
Patient completed 14-day course of cefepime on ___.  He will 
need blood cultures drawn on ___ (two weeks after completion 
of anitbiotics) to assess for efficacy of therapy.  If blood 
cultures are negative, he will have another tunneled line 
placed.

# Multifocal pneumonia: CT torso on ___ showed evidence of 
multifocal pneumonia; vancomycin was added to cefepime.  He was 
treated with this combination of antibiotics through ___ for 
an 8-day course of treatment.  After initial hypoxia to the high 
___, he returned to his baseline, satting in the low ___ on 4L 
NC (home supplemental oxygen requirement) on ___.  His 
respiratory status remained stable, and he was afebrile for the 
remainder of his admission.

# Acute kidney injury: Prerenal versus HRS Type 2.  Patient was 
noted to have creatinine increased to 1.7 on admission, 
increased from his baseline of 1.3 on ___.  This was thought 
to be secondary to volume depletion compounded by diuretic use.  
With initial pressor and volume support, creatinine improved 
rapidly to 1.1.  He was subsequently diuresed with IV diuretics 
for volume overload on ___ and ___, and resumed oral diuretics. 
 His creatinine increased again on ___ to 1.5, which may 
have indicated HRS Type 2 in the setting of poorer functional 
reserve from infections.  Diuretics were discontinued, and he 
was treated with aggressive albumin repletion.  At the time of 
discharge, creatinine had trended down and remained stable at 
1.5.  This may be near his new baseline.  Oral diuretics should 
be restarted at the discretion of his outpatient providers.

# Recurrent ascites: Patient's HCV cirrhosis had been 
complicated by ascites in the past, but recently well-controlled 
on diuretics.  Ascites likely occurred during this admission in 
the context of infection, then recurred due to adjustment and 
holding of diuretic medications due to ___.  He underwent 
diagnostic paracentesis on ___, then therapeutic paracentesis 
on ___ (5L removed), ___ (6L removed), ___ (3L 
removed), and ___ (6L removed).  All fluid did not have 
evidence of SBP.  Paracenteses on ___ and ___ were 
complicated by persistent leak, requiring sutures, ostomy bag 
for fluid collection and Dermabond.  Dermabond effectively 
stopped the leak.  Patient is scheduled for outpatient 
ultrasound-guided paracentesis on ___.  He will resume oral 
diuretics at the discretion of his hepatologist after discharge.

# Portopulmonary hypertension: Chronic, on sildenafil and 
Remodulin infusion. Oxygen level 88%RA on arrival, normally uses 
4L oxygen at home.  Has history of portopulmonary HTN for which 
he is on remodulin infusion pump. Dyspnea likely from increasing 
ascites and pulmonary edema. Respiratory status improved, and he 
was satting low ___ by ___. TTE on ___ showed increased 
pulmonary hypertension from 46 (on previous echo) to 66, EF 
>55%, mild LVOT. Pulmonary thought this to be likely secondary 
to right heart overload and recommended diuresis. Additionally, 
as described above CT, did demonstrate a multi-focal PNA which 
may also be contibuting. He was kept on his remodulin and 
sildenafil was restarted ___. He continued these medications 
throughout the remainder of his admission, and was satting in 
the mid-90s on room air and ___ NC at the time of discharge.

CHRONIC ISSUES:
# HCV Cirrhosis: Complicated by hepatic encephalopathy, varices, 
ascites, hepatorenal syndrome and portopulmonary hypertension, 
on the transplant list. During acute illness, MELD score 
fluctuated somewhat due to bilirubin peaking at 2.8, creatinine 
peaking at 1.7,   At the end of his hospitalization, MELD score 
was consistently 17.  As noted above, he required multiple 
therapeutic paracenteses on  ___ and ___ for recurrent

# Pancytopenia: Chronic, has been followed by

# Depression: Outpatient Prozac had been stopped early in

INDICATION:  Liver failure with worsening ascites.  Evaluate for portal vein
thrombosis.

COMPARISON:  Multiple abdominal ultrasound examinations dating back to ___ as well as multiple CT abdomen and pelvis studies dating back to
___.

TECHNIQUE:  Grayscale and Doppler ultrasound images were obtained of the
abdomen.

FINDINGS:  The liver is nodular and coarse in echotexture, compatible with
known cirrhosis.  No worrisome focal lesions are identified.  There is no
intra- or extra-hepatic biliary duct dilatation, and the common bile duct
measures 5 mm in diameter.  The gallbladder is absent.  The pancreas is not
well visualized due to overlying bowel gas.  The main, right and left portal
veins are patent with hepatopetal flow.  Extensive varices are visualized
throughout the abdomen.  The spleen is massively enlarged measuring 24 cm in
longest axis, but has a homogeneous echotexture.  Large volume ascites is
identified.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Main, right, and left portal vein are patent with hepatopetal flow,
without evidence of thrombosis.
2.  Course, nodular liver, extensive splenomegaly, extensive varices and large
volume ascites, compatible with cirrhosis with portal hypertension.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Evaluation of the patient with gram-negative
bacteremia and now with new left internal jugular line placement.

AP radiograph of the chest was reviewed in comparison to ___
obtained at 09:27 a.m.

The left internal jugular line ,recently inserted, terminates at the
cavoatrial junction.  The right central venous line that potentially reflects
a Hickman catheter or hemodialysis terminates in the right atrium
approximately 5 cm below the cavoatrial junction.  There is no pneumothorax. 
As compared to the prior study, there is substantial interval increase in
pulmonary edema as well as in multifocal opacities that might reflect
progression of infectious process.  Small bilateral pleural effusion is
re-demonstrated.  There is no evidence of pneumothorax.

REASON FOR EXAMINATION:  Evaluation of the patient with hypoxia.

AP radiograph of the chest was reviewed in comparison to prior study obtained
___ at 9:43 p.m.

Since the prior study, there has been interval improvement of pulmonary edema.
Bibasilar consolidations are unchanged.  The position of tubes and lines is
unchanged.  The confluent opacity in the right lower lung is concerning for
right lower lobe pneumonia.

INDICATION:  Patient has an indwelling right IJ Hickman catheter for treatment
for pulmonary hypertension.  There is clinical suspicion that the catheter is
now infected and removal was requested.

PHYSICIAN:  ___, M.D., fellow, performed the procedure.  Dr. ___
___, M.D., resident, performed the procedure.

PROCEDURES:  Removal of tunneled access line.

PROCEDURE DETAILS:  The patient was positioned supine.  The area was prepped
and draped in sterile fashion.  Timeout was performed.

Local anesthesia was applied with lidocaine at the tunnel exit site and along
the tunnel.  The catheter did not come out with gentle traction after the
retention suture was cut.  For this reason, blunt dissection was used in the
tunnel to free up the cuff from the surrounding tissues.  After some further
dissection and traction of the line, the catheter was removed intact and the
tip was sent for culture.  Pressure was applied with good hemostasis and a
dressing was placed.  There were no complications.

CONCLUSION:  Uncomplicated removal of a tunneled access line from the right
internal jugular vein with the catheter tip sent for culture.

INDICATION:  History of HCV cirrhosis, presenting with Gram-negative rod
bacteremia.  Evaluate for source of infection.

COMPARISON:  CTA chest from ___.  CT abdomen and pelvis from
___.

TECHNIQUE:  MDCT axial images were acquired through the chest, abdomen, and
pelvis following the administration of oral contrast material only. 
Multiplanar reformats were performed.

TOTAL DLP:  1019 mGy-cm.

CHEST CT:  The visualized portion of the thyroid gland is unremarkable.  Lack
of intravenous contrast material limits assessment for mediastinal and hilar
lymphadenopathy.  An 11 mm upper right paratracheal node is minimally
increased in size compared to CT from ___ (2:15).  Heavily
calcified left hilar nodes measuring up to 16 x 16 mm are not significantly
changed in size compared to the prior CT from ___.  The thoracic
aorta is normal in caliber.  Although assessment is limited given the
non-contrast technique, the main pulmonary artery and right/left main
pulmonary arteries are mildly dilated, suggestive of pulmonary arterial
hypertension, not significantly changed compared to CT from ___.
The heart is mildly enlarged, as before.  A left internal jugular central
venous catheter ends in the upper right atrium.  A tunneled right internal
jugular central venous catheter ends near the superior cavoatrial junction. 
Known paraesophageal varices are not well assessed on the present study,
better seen on the contrast-enhanced study from ___.

There are widespread peribronchovascular ground-glass opacities throughout
both lungs, markedly increased compared to the prior CT from ___, likely infectious in nature.  More consolidative opacities are seen
within the dependent aspects of both lower lobes, likely some combination of
atelectasis and infection.  There are small bilateral non-hemorrhagic pleural
effusions, right greater than left, new compared to the most recent CT from
___.  Tiny left lower lobe calcified granulomas are noted.  The
airways are patent to the segmental level bilaterally.

ABDOMEN CT:  Lack of intravenous contrast material limits assessment of the
abdominal organs.  The liver is nodular in contour, in keeping with known
cirrhosis.  The patient is status post cholecystectomy.  The spleen is
massively enlarged, measuring up to 24.1 cm in its greatest axial dimension,
not significantly changed compared to CT from ___.  Multiple
punctate calcifications throughout the spleen are consistent with prior
granulomatous disease, not significantly changed.  The pancreas and left
adrenal gland are not well assessed.  The right adrenal gland is normal.  A
2.2 cm high-density lesion extending from the posterolateral aspect of the
right kidney is consistent with a hemorrhagic versus proteinaceous cyst, not
significantly changed in size compared to CT from ___, better
characterized on the multiphasic study from ___ given its lack of
enhancement on post-contrast images.  The kidneys are otherwise unremarkable. 
The lower thoracic esophagus is mildly patulous.  Limited assessment of the
small bowel and colon is unremarkable.  There is a moderate-to-large quantity
of ascites, markedly increased compared to CT from ___.  The
degree of edema within the central mesentery is also increased.  Evaluation
for enlarged abdominal lymph nodes is limited given the non-contrast
technique.  Massive perisplenic and perigastric varices were better evaluated
on the contrast-enhanced study from ___.  Scattered aortic
calcifications are seen.

PELVIS CT:  The bladder is collapsed around a Foley catheter.  There are no
definite pathologically enlarged pelvic lymph nodes.  Moderate-to-large volume
ascites was already discussed.

SOFT TISSUES AND BONES.  There is marked anasarca.  No suspicious lytic or
blastic lesions are identified.  There is evidence of prior vertebroplasties
involving the L2 through L4 levels with unchanged loss of height of the
vertebral bodies along the same distribution.  Grade 1 retrolisthesis of L4 on
L5 and grade 1 anterolisthesis of L3 and L4 are not significantly changed. 
There has been a prior laminectomy at L5 with posterior fusion across L5-S1
with pedicular screws and spinal rods, not significantly changed.  An
intervertebral disc space fusion device is seen at L5-S1, not significantly
changed in position.  Compression deformities throughout the thoracic and
upper lumbar spine are not significantly changed compared to CT from ___ and ___.  A non-displaced fracture through the mid
portion of the sternum is new compared to CT from ___ (301B:43),
age indeterminate in nature.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Bilateral multifocal pneumonia, fully described above.  Small bilateral
pleural effusions, right greater than left, new compared to prior CT from
___.

2.  Cirrhotic liver with evidence of portal hypertension including
large-volume ascites, massive splenomegaly, perigastric/splenic varices, and
paraesophageal varices.  The degree of ascites has markedly increased compared
to the prior CT from ___ but the splanchnic vasculature all
remains patent.

3.  Marked anasarca, new compared to the prior CT from ___.

4.  Mild dilatation of the main pulmonary artery and its central branches,
suggestive of pulmonary arterial hypertension, as seen on prior chest CT from
___.

5.  Non-displaced fracture through the mid sternum, new compared to CT from
___, age indeterminate.  Clinical correlation recommended.

6.  Multilevel thoracolumbar spine compression deformities, similar in
appearance compared to prior CT.

7.  Calcified left hilar lymph nodes, left lower lobe calcified granulomas,
and punctate calcifications throughout the spleen, suggestive of prior
granulomatous disease.

CLINICAL HISTORY:  Hepatitis C cirrhosis, hepatic encephalopathy, ascites.

Plain film shows extensive ascites, though the actual amount is somewhat
difficult to assess.  The bowel gas patten is unremarkable.  There is no
evidence of obstruction or ileus.

HISTORY:  New hepatitis-C virus cirrhosis on transplant list a/w bacteremia,
worsening ascites, pneumonia, and SBP.  

COMPARISON:  CT torso ___.  

PROCEDURE:

The procedure, risks, benefits, and alternatives were discussed with the
patient and written informed consent was obtained.

A pre-procedure time-out was performed, discussing the planned procedure,
confirming the patient's identity with three identifiers, and reviewing a
checklist per ___ protocol.

Under ultrasound guidance, the largest pocket of ascitic fluid was identified
and a site was marked.  The skin was prepped and draped in the usual sterile
fashion.  10 mL of 1% lidocaine was instilled into the subcutaneous tissues
for local anesthesia.

A ___ ___ catheter was advanced into the largest fluid pocket in the
left mid abdomen and 5 L of straw-colored ascitic fluid was removed.  Ascitic
fluid continued to leak from the puncture site after removal of the catheter
and the site was closed with a single ___ silk suture.  

Samples of ascitic fluid were sent to the laboratory for the requested
studies.  The patient tolerated the procedure well without immediate
complication.  Estimated blood loss was minimal.

Dr. ___ attending radiologist, was present for the critical portions
of the procedure. 

FINDINGS:

There is a large amount of ascites seen in the abdomen. The largest fluid
pocket, in the left mid abdomen was targeted for paracentesis. 

IMPRESSION:

1. Ultrasound-guided therapeutic and diagnostic paracentesis with removal of 5
L of straw-colored ascitic fluid.  Samples of fluid were sent to the
laboratory for the requested studies.  

2. The puncture site was closed with a single 5 0 silk suture to stop leakage
of ascitic fluid.

HISTORY:  ___ year old man with HCV cirrhosis REASON FOR THIS EXAMINATION: 6L
paracentesis, please perform on ___ 

COMPARISON:  Paracentesis ___ 

FINDINGS:

PROCEDURE:

The risks and benefits of the procedure were explained to the patient, and
written informed consent was obtained.  Preprocedure time out was performed
verifying 3 patient identifiers and the nature of the procedure to be
performed.  Preprocedure limited ultrasound demonstrated a moderate amount of
ascites in the bilateral lower quadrants, the left lower quadrant was targeted
for therapeutic paracentesis.  The skin overlying the left lower quadrant was
prepped and draped in standard sterile fashion.  Local anesthesia was achieved
via subcutaneous injection of approximately 6 cc of 1% lidocaine.  Under
direct ultrasonographic guidance, a 5 ___ ___ needle was advanced into the
left lower quadrant fluid pocket, the catheter was advanced and the needle was
removed.  The catheter was connected to low wall suction.  A total of
approximately 6 L of reddish ascites was evacuated.  The patient tolerated the
procedure well, with no complications evident at the time of the procedure. 
The attending radiologist, Dr. ___, was present and supervising throughout
the procedure.   

IMPRESSION:

Technically successful ultrasound-guided therapeutic paracentesis.  Total of 6
L of reddish ascites evacuated.

HISTORY:  ___ man with new PICC.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  New right-sided PICC terminates at approximately the cavoatrial
junction. A left-sided IJ terminates in the right atrium, unchanged. 
Multifocal bilateral opacities are again present, consistent with atelectasis
but also pneumonia should be considered.  No pneumothorax.

HISTORY:  ___ male with HCV cirrhosis, recurrent ascites, and acute
kidney injury.

COMPARISON:  ___.  

PROCEDURE:

After discussion of the risks, benefits, and alternatives to the procedure,
written informed consent was obtained from the patient.  A pre-procedure time
out was performed per ___ protocol, confirming 3 patient identifiers, the
procedure to be performed, patient's laboratory results, patient allergies,
and specimens to be sent.  Due to thrombocytopenia, platelets were
administered during the procedure and the patient's hemodynamic parameters
were monitored by radiology nursing staff.

Under ultrasound guidance, a pocket of ascites in the right lower quadrant was
identified and the skin was marked.  The patient was prepped and draped in the
usual sterile fashion.  Local anesthesia was provided with subcutaneous
injection of 1% lidocaine.  A ___ ___ catheter was introduced into the
peritoneal cavity.  20 cc of peritoneal fluid was aspirated and sent to the
lab for analysis per request of the clinical team.  6 Liters of clear yellow
peritoneal fluid was subsequently aspirated per maximum volume specified by
the clinical team.  The catheter was removed and hemostasis was achieved with
direct pressure.  A sterile dressing was applied.  The procedure was well
tolerated without immediate complication.  The attending radiologist, Dr.
___ was present and supervising throughout the procedure.  

IMPRESSION:

Technically successful ultrasound-guided diagnostic and therapeutic
paracentesis.
